title: Class one entry age at government schools rises to six from 2027
excerpt: The change brings government secondary schools in line with private schools and the 2010 education policy. Lottery admission for class one stays.
content:
Children must be at least six to enter class one at government secondary schools from the 2027 school year, up from five, under a revised admission policy from the Ministry of Education, The Daily Star reported on 13 November.

What changes

  • Age: applicants must be six or older, and under seven, on 1 January 2027, the newspaper reported.
  • Why: the National Education Policy 2010 sets six as the standard entry age, according to the report. A separate policy for private schools, issued on 10 November, already set the minimum at six.
  • Special needs: children with special needs can get an age relaxation of up to five years, and 2% of seats are reserved for them.
  • Proof of age: an attested copy of the online birth registration certificate.
  • Selection: class one places are still filled by digital lottery. Classes two to nine use written tests based on the previous year's textbooks.

Other seat quotas stay: 5% for children of freedom fighters, 3% for siblings, 2% for twins and 2% for children of eligible education ministry staff. In Dhaka city, 40% of seats are kept for children living in set catchment areas. Each section can take up to 55 students.

The policy applies to government secondary schools. The report does not say whether government primary schools, run by the Directorate of Primary Education, will follow the same rule, or how many children are affected.

Why it matters

Some children who would have started class one in 2027 at five will now wait a year. NGOs that run pre-primary and early learning centres, and those supporting children with disabilities, may see more five-year-olds needing a place. Families without an online birth certificate could struggle to apply, so birth registration support remains important.

What to watch

The admission lottery timetable for 2027, and whether the Directorate of Primary Education and NGO-run schools adopt the same age rule.
